Read on drafting, and read again on review.** The `paper-authoring`\n4\tskill and the `prose-reviewer` agent both consume this file, so a rule cannot mean one\n5\tthing while writing and another while reviewing.\n6\t\n7\t⚠️ **This is the shared FLOOR, not the whole review.** The reviewer additionally carries\n8\treader-outcome questions that do not appear here and that an author must never be given as\n9\ta checklist: a generator optimises against any list it can see. See the skill's §\"Why the\n10\treviewer knows things this file does not\".\n11\t\n12\tEvery rule below was derived from a measured sweep of the 21-bundle corpus, not from a\n13\tstyle guide. Where a number appears, it is what was counted.\n14\t\n15\t---\n16\t\n17\t## 1. The em-dash: prohibited outright, including in headings\n18\t\n19\t**Never write `---` or a literal `—`.** Two forms exist and both are banned.\n20\t\n21\t**Why this one is absolute.** An em-dash reads as machine-authored to a 2026 reader and\n22\tcosts trust before the physics is evaluated. One is as disqualifying as forty, so there is\n23\tno acceptable density. Enforced by `validate.py --check bundle_prose_em_dash_free`, target\n24\tzero. Measured before the corpus was swept: **741 of them, and 0 of 21 bundles clean.**\n25\t\n26\t### ⚠️ The en-dash `--` is MANDATORY and must never be touched\n27\t\n28\t`--` (exactly two hyphens) is a different character doing a different job, and the corpus\n29\tcarries **1,121** of them:\n30\t\n31\t- compound eponyms: `Bose--Einstein`, `Bekenstein--Hawking`, `Schwinger--Keldysh`,\n32\t  `Kaul--Majumdar`, `Chowdhury--Hartnoll--Hebbar--Khondaker`, `SK--EFT`\n33\t- numeric ranges: `pp. 10--15`, `$2$--$3$ K`\n34\t\n35\t**An author over-correcting to \"no dashes at all\" breaks every compound name in the\n36\tprogram, and the check cannot see it** because it counts exactly three hyphens. This is the\n37\tsingle highest-cost mistake available here. One live line contained both:\n38\t`observables---also drives the SK--EFT`.\n39\t\n40\tA third variant exists in the wild: the literal Unicode en-dash `–` (U+2013), found as\n41\t`Kaul–Majumdar` and `Chowdhury–Hartnoll–Hebbar–Khondaker`. Write `--` instead; D3 once\n42\tspelled the same name both ways.\n43\t\n44\t### Replacing an em-dash is a REWRITE, not a substitution\n45\t\n46\tA mechanical swap produces comma splices. Identify the job the dash was doing, then use the\n47\tpunctuation that already exists for that job. Frequencies below are from six independent\n48\treadings of all 741 occurrences.\n49\t\n50\t| The dash was doing | Frequency | Write instead |\n51\t|---|---|---|\n52\t| Paired aside interrupting a clause | ~45–55% | parentheses; a comma pair when the aside is short and contains no commas of its own |\n53\t| Introducing an explanation, expansion or list | ~30–45% | a colon |\n54\t| Separating a label from its gloss in `\\item`, `\\subsection{}`, `\\paragraph{}` | ~15% | a colon, always |\n55\t| Contrastive \"X, not Y\" interjection | ~7% | a comma pair (parentheses would demote a correction to an aside) |\n56\t| Joining two independent clauses | ~3–15% | a semicolon, or a full stop and a new sentence |\n57\t| Trailing appositive glossing a number's significance | common in E1/E2 | a comma |\n58\t\n59\t### The four hard cases, each of which defeats a mechanical fix\n60\t\n61\t1. **The aside contains its own parenthetical or citation.** Converting the outer dash to\n62\t   parentheses yields stacked or nested parens that read as a stutter:\n63\t   `(\\lean{diamondDist_eq_choiSDP}) (the Watrous semidefinite program~\\cite{Watrous2018}) is proven`.\n64\t   **Merge the tag and the aside into ONE parenthetical** with an internal comma or\n65\t   semicolon. Do not nest.\n66\t2. **The aside contains a comma-separated list.** Comma-punctuating it makes the reader\n67\t   parse the inner items as continuing the outer sentence's list. Use parentheses.\n68\t3. **The sentence already has a colon later on.** Adding a second colon reads as a nested\n69\t   label. Restructure with a copula: `X is the headline theorem: Y`.\n70\t4. **Three levels of subordination.** An aside inside an aside inside a main clause is a\n71\t   sentence trying to be three sentences. Split it.\n72\t\n73\t### The generative habits behind them: prohibit these, not just the symbol\n74\t\n75\tAll six readers converged on the same root, so treat it as the rule that matters:\n76\t\n77\t> **Do not interrupt a main clause to insert a clarification.** Write the clarification as\n78\t> its own sentence, before or after.\n79\t\n80\tThe dominant shape was *claim, dash, restatement-with-a-twist, dash, continuation*: draft a\n81\tclean declarative, then, worried a reader will misattribute a convention or miss a caveat,\n82\tsplice the qualifier into the middle. It concentrated in exactly the paragraphs doing the\n83\theaviest epistemic hedging (novelty disclaimers, provenance caveats, convention-pinning),\n84\twhich is where this project's prose is densest.\n85\t\n86\tFour more shapes, each of which reliably produces an em-dash:\n87\t\n88\t- **Name-then-gloss in itemised lists.** `\\item \\verb|foo_bar|: the substantive witness`.\n89\t  Use the colon from the start; this was the single most common pattern in the Lean-heavy\n90\t  bundles.\n91\t- **Label-then-gloss in headings.** `\\subsection{Pillar 1: Golterman--Shamir}`. A dash in a\n92\t  heading also reads as a tic when scanning the table of contents.\n93\t- **Tag-stacking.** A claim ending in a `\\lean{...}` identifier in parens, then a dash\n94\t  glossing that identifier. This is an appositive that got dash-punctuated only because the\n95\t  sentence had already spent its parentheses.\n96\t- **Claim-then-immediately-re-scope.** `T_H \\approx 2.4$ K --- nine orders of magnitude\n97\t  above atomic BEC --- with adiabaticity...`. A defensible instinct for a rigorous program,\n98\t  executed with the wrong punctuation: pick the syntax that matches the qualifier's\n99\t  grammatical role.\n100\t\n101\t---\n102\t\n103\t## 2. A fix may not narrate itself\n104\t\n105\t**Never tell the reader what an earlier draft of this paper said, when it was corrected, or\n106\twhich review round caught it.** A referee has no access to that process and cannot act on\n107\tit; the text reads as a changelog pasted into a manuscript.\n108\t\n109\tEnforced by `validate.py --check bundle_reader_facing_voice`, target zero. Banned forms:\n110\t\n111\t- a correction stamped with a date: `(corrected 2026-08-01)`\n112\t- an account of an earlier draft: `three earlier drafts of this paragraph asserted...`\n113\t- a first-person superseded claim: `We previously shipped a theorem asserting...`\n114\t- an internal review reference: `(D11 Stage-13 round-14 finding 6.2)`\n115\t- the project's own planning documents: `Our earlier planning documents described...`\n116\t- review rounds cast as actors: `rounds 7 and 10 both rated this cosmetic`\n117\t- a claim about the paper's own drafting: `typeset unconditionally in every draft`\n118\t\n119\t**The history is not lost, it moves.** `papers/<X>/change_log.md` and\n120\t`docs/review_finding_supersessions.json` are where a later reader can actually check it, and\n121\tthe ledger entry is required by the lift procedure anyway.\n122\t\n123\t### ⚠️ Removing narration is not deleting content\n124\t\n125\tMost of these passages wrap something real, and the substance must survive:\n126\t\n127\t- **A retraction is a scientific disclosure.** Restate it as a present-tense negative\n128\t  result: what is *not* claimed and why it fails. Do not delete the paragraph.\n129\t- **A scope correction states the correct scope.** Keep every factual statement about what\n130\t  a module does and does not contain, including file:line references. Drop only \"earlier\n131\t  drafts called it X\" and the date/round/finding tag.\n132\t- **A completeness disclaimer is a real caveat.** Keep it; drop the account of what two\n133\t  earlier drafts asserted.\n134\t\n135\t### What is NOT prohibited\n136\t\n137\tReporting that *the literature* corrected something is ordinary scholarship: `Smith\n138\tcorrected this coefficient in 2019` is correct and stays.\n139\t\n140\tDescribing the verification pipeline is legitimate **when the pipeline is the paper's\n141\tsubject matter** (I1, and I2/I3 for library conventions). Addressing the paper's own\n142\treferees is legitimate anywhere: `lets Mathlib4 reviewers calibrate expectations`.\n143\t\n144\tThis distinction is why the rule targets the *act* of self-narration rather than a\n145\tvocabulary. A word list banning `Stage 13`, `reviewer` and `adversarial review` scores 90\n146\thits on this corpus, of which 48 are legitimate uses in the methodology paper alone.\n147\t\n148\t---\n149\t\n150\t## 3. Claim discipline\n151\t\n152\tThese are enforced elsewhere in the pipeline; they are repeated here because they are\n153\tcheaper to satisfy while drafting than to repair at review.\n154\t\n155\t- **Never hedge a count or numerical literal with \"alt convention\" or \"+N depending on\n156\t  convention\" without proving the convention sensitivity.** If counts disagree across\n157\t  tools, find the truth. Convention-drift framing masks actual content drift: a \"161 ± 3\n158\t  alt convention\" was really 164, and the +3 was real drift.\n159\t- **Verify which registry a name lives in before citing it.** `AXIOM_METADATA`,\n160\t  `PLACEHOLDER_THEOREMS`, `HYPOTHESIS_REGISTRY` and `BORDISM_HYPOTHESES` are four different\n161\t  tables; a name found in one and attributed to another is a Stage-13 blocker.\n162\t- **Every cross-language prior-art claim must resolve to a verifiable URL or canonical\n163\t  ecosystem reference.** Hallucinated libraries have shipped before. When in doubt, cite\n164\t  the ecosystem (UniMath, Mathlib4) rather than naming a specific library.\n165\t- **When broadening an attribution, verify every addition belongs in the broadened\n166\t  category.** Surface code is abelian-stabiliser QEC, not non-Abelian-anyon TQC.\n167\t- **Numbers come from the pipeline.** Use `\\input{tables/<spec>.tex}` and the `counts.tex`\n168\t  macros rather than typing a literal.\n169\t\n170\t---\n171\t\n172\t## 4. Structure\n173\t\n174\t- **The abstract leads with the result**, not with the programme, the architecture, or what\n175\t  the paper will do.\n176\t- **The reader never sees the project's internal taxonomy.** Not `bundle`, `tier`, `wave`,\n177\t  `phase`, or `splash`. Provides the house voice, the prohibited-pattern floor, and venue conventions for SK-EFT Hawking publication bundles.\n4\t---\n5\t\n6\t# Authoring a publication bundle\n7\t\n8\tGuidance for writing manuscript prose in `papers/<bundle>/paper_draft.tex`. This is the\n9\tgenerative counterpart to the `prose-reviewer` agent; both read the same prohibited-pattern\n10\treference so a rule cannot drift between writing and review.\n11\t\n12\tRead it either way you draft: the lead writing in-context, or a `paper-drafter` agent\n13\tdispatched over one section. `paper-drafter` reads this file and the same reference by\n14\tpath, so the floor is identical however the prose is produced.\n15\t\n16\t**Read `references/prohibited-patterns.md` before drafting.** It is mandatory, not\n17\tbackground, and it is short.\n18\t\n19\t---\n20\t\n21\t## Why this skill exists\n22\t\n23\tThe pipeline had three reviewer agents and no authoring guidance. Everything about how to\n24\twrite lived in `docs/BUNDLE_LIFT_PROCEDURE.md` §7 as a bookkeeping checklist consulted at\n25\tlift time. The measured result of that gap, across 21 bundles:\n26\t\n27\t- **741 em-dashes**, with zero bundles clean\n28\t- **13 passages** narrating the paper's own correction history to a referee\n29\t- **9 of 21 bundles shipping zero figures**, because the lift step only migrated figures\n30\t  that already existed and no step ever planned one\n31\t- **D3 carrying 37 sections against 31 contributing sources**, which is sedimentation\n32\t  rather than architecture\n33\t\n34\tNone of that is a capability limit. It is what an unguided generator produces when the only\n35\tcontrols are downstream reviewers.\n36\t\n37\t---\n38\t\n39\t## Before writing a section\n40\t\n41\t1. **Read the charter.** `papers/<X>/bundle_metadata.json` carries `target_journal` and\n42\t   `length_target`; the section belongs to a planned outline, not to a source paper that\n43\t   happened to be registered.\n44\t2. **Read the substrate directly.** Contributing per-paper drafts, the Lean modules, the\n45\t   roadmap. Do not write from a summary.\n46\t3. **Know the claim this section makes** and which apex theorem backs it. Real.pi * p.α_ADW)\n303\t\n304\ttheorem M_c_pos (p : ADWParams) : 0 < M_c p := by\n305\t  unfold M_c\n306\t  have hπ : (0 : ℝ) < Real.pi := Real.pi_pos\n307\t  have hnum : 0 < p.N_f * p.Λ_UV := mul_pos p.N_pos p.Λ_pos\n308\t  have hden : 0 < 12 * Real.pi * p.α_ADW :=\n309\t    mul_pos (by positivity) p.α_pos\n310\t  exact div_pos hnum hden\n311\t\n312\t/--\n313\t**Decidable regime classifier.** Returns the regime of a given BH at\n314\tthe given ADW substrate by comparing `M` against the critical mass `M_c`.\n315\t\n316\t**Anti-pattern audit.** Function, not existential.\n317\t-/\n318\tnoncomputable def classify (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) : Regime :=\n319\t  if b.M > M_c p then .Schwarzschild\n320\t  else if b.M < M_c p then .ADWExtremality\n321\t  else .Boundary\n322\t\n323\ttheorem classify_Schwarzschild_iff\n324\t    (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) :\n325\t    classify b p = .Schwarzschild ↔ b.M > M_c p := by\n326\t  unfold classify\n327\t  by_cases h : b.M > M_c p\n328\t  · simp [h]\n329\t  · simp only [h, if_false]\n330\t    by_cases h2 : b.M < M_c p\n331\t    · simp [h2]\n332\t    · simp [h2]\n333\t\n334\ttheorem classify_ADWExtremality_iff\n335\t    (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) :\n336\t    classify b p = .ADWExtremality ↔ b.M < M_c p := by\n337\t  unfold classify\n338\t  by_cases h : b.M > M_c p\n339\t  · have hne : ¬ b.M < M_c p := not_lt.mpr (le_of_lt h)\n340\t    simp [h, hne]\n341\t  · simp only [h, if_false]\n342\t    by_cases h2 : b.M < M_c p\n343\t    · simp [h2]\n344\t    · simp [h2]\n345\t\n346\ttheorem classify_Boundary_iff\n347\t    (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) :\n348\t    classify b p = .Boundary ↔ b.M = M_c p := by\n349\t  unfold classify\n350\t  by_cases h : b.M > M_c p\n351\t  · have hne : b.M ≠ M_c p := ne_of_gt h\n352\t    simp [h, hne]\n353\t  · simp only [h, if_false]\n354\t    by_cases h2 : b.M < M_c p\n355\t    · have hne : b.M ≠ M_c p := ne_of_lt h2\n356\t      simp [h2, hne]\n357\t    · simp only [h2, if_false]\n358\t      have h_le : b.M ≤ M_c p := not_lt.mp h\n359\t      have h_ge : M_c p ≤ b.M := not_lt.mp h2\n360\t      exact ⟨fun _ => le_antisymm h_le h_ge, fun _ => trivial⟩\n361\t\n362\t/-! ## §4 — Time-evolution Hawking-temperature forms\n363\t\n364\tTwo evaporation-evolution profiles per regime, each anchored to its\n365\tprimary source. Both are non-trivial functions of their inputs (no\n366\ttrivial-projection); both are positive on their physical domains.\n367\t-/\n368\t\n369\t/--\n370\t**Acoustic Hawking temperature time evolution.** Leading-order\n371\texponential decay form per the project's own\n372\t`src/wkb/backreaction.py` (line 449-450), citing Balbinot 2005:\n373\t\n374\t    T_H_acoustic_evolution(T_H,0, τ_cool, t) = T_H,0 · exp(-t / τ_cool)\n375\t\n376\tThe exponential is the leading-order approximation to the full coupled\n377\tbackreaction equations of Balbinot 2005 §\"The fate of the acoustic\n378\tblack hole\" (Eq. Tsonic + extrapolation `t ~ 1/T³`); the full\n379\tbackreaction.py uses the coupled ODE rather than the exponential, but\n380\tboth share `dT/dt < 0` and asymptotic `T → 0`.\n381\t-/\n382\tnoncomputable def T_H_acoustic_evolution (T_H0 τ_cool t : ℝ) : ℝ :=\n383\t  T_H0 * Real.exp (-t / τ_cool)\n384\t\n385\t/-- At `t = 0` the acoustic profile equals its initial value `T_H,0`. -/\n386\ttheorem T_H_acoustic_evolution_at_zero (T_H0 τ_cool : ℝ) :\n387\t    T_H_acoustic_evolution T_H0 τ_cool 0 = T_H0 := by\n388\t  unfold T_H_acoustic_evolution\n389\t  rw [neg_zero, zero_div, Real.exp_zero, mul_one]\n390\t\n391\t/-- Positivity of the acoustic profile when `T_H,0 > 0`. -/\n392\ttheorem T_H_acoustic_evolution_pos {T_H0 : ℝ} (hT0 : 0 < T_H0)\n393\t    (τ_cool t : ℝ) : 0 < T_H_acoustic_evolution T_H0 τ_cool t := by\n394\t  unfold T_H_acoustic_evolution\n395\t  exact mul_pos hT0 (Real.exp_pos _)\n396\t\n397\t/-- **Strict monotone-decay** (Balbinot 2005 Eq. Tsonic content): for\n398\tpositive `T_H,0` and `τ_cool`, `T_H(t)` is strictly decreasing in `t`.\n399\tThis is the load-bearing primary-source claim for the acoustic\n400\tregime: `dT/dt < 0` strictly, formalized as monotone-decreasing. -/\n401\ttheorem T_H_acoustic_evolution_strict_decreasing {T_H0 τ_cool : ℝ}\n402\t    (hT0 : 0 < T_H0) (hτ : 0 < τ_cool)\n403\t    {t₁ t₂ : ℝ} (h : t₁ < t₂) :\n404\t    T_H_acoustic_evolution T_H0 τ_cool t₂ < T_H_acoustic_evolution T_H0 τ_cool t₁ := by\n405\t  unfold T_H_acoustic_evolution\n406\t  have h_arg : -t₂ / τ_cool < -t₁ / τ_cool := by\n407\t    apply (div_lt_div_iff_of_pos_right hτ).mpr\n408\t    linarith\n409\t  have h_exp : Real.exp (-t₂ / τ_cool) < Real.exp (-t₁ / τ_cool) :=\n410\t    Real.exp_lt_exp.mpr h_arg\n411\t  exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left h_exp hT0\n412\t\n413\t/--\n414\t**Schwarzschild Hawking temperature.** Textbook form `T_H = ℏ/(8π M)`\n415\t(Hawking 1975); we work in natural units `ℏ = 1`. Function of bulk\n416\tmass M only.\n417\t-/\n418\tnoncomputable def T_H_schwarzschild (M : ℝ) : ℝ :=\n419\t  1 / (8 * Real.pi * M)\n420\t\n421\ttheorem T_H_schwarzschild_pos {M : ℝ} (hM : 0 < M) :\n422\t    0 < T_H_schwarzschild M := by\n423\t  unfold T_H_schwarzschild\n424\t  have hπ : (0 : ℝ) < Real.pi := Real.pi_pos\n425\t  exact div_pos one_pos (by positivity)\n426\t\n427\t/-- **Schwarzschild T_H is strictly decreasing in M.** Standard\n428\tHawking-1975 result. During evaporation `dM/dt < 0`, so combined with\n429\tthis monotonicity gives `dT_H/dt > 0` — the \"heating as evaporates\"\n430\tregime sign. -/\n431\ttheorem T_H_schwarzschild_strict_decreasing\n432\t    {M₁ M₂ : ℝ} (hM₁ : 0 < M₁) (h : M₁ < M₂) :\n433\t    T_H_schwarzschild M₂ < T_H_schwarzschild M₁ := by\n434\t  unfold T_H_schwarzschild\n435\t  have hπ : (0 : ℝ) < Real.pi := Real.pi_pos\n436\t  have hM₂ : 0 < M₂ := lt_trans hM₁ h\n437\t  have hd₁ : 0 < 8 * Real.pi * M₁ := by positivity\n438\t  have hd₂ : 0 < 8 * Real.pi * M₂ := by positivity\n439\t  have hdens : 8 * Real.pi * M₁ < 8 * Real.pi * M₂ := by\n440\t    have : 8 * Real.pi > 0 := by positivity\n441\t    nlinarith\n442\t  exact one_div_lt_one_div_of_lt hd₁ hdens\n443\t\n444\t/-! ## §5 — SK-EFT second law (Glorioso–Liu, no NEC) -/\n445\t\n446\t/--\n447\t**Wave 5 second-law Prop bundle (post-Stage-13 strengthened).**\n448\tEncodes the Glorioso–Liu theorem (arXiv:1612.07705, §III, Eq. 3.20):\n449\tdynamical KMS Z₂ symmetry + unitarity (Im S_eff ≥ 0) imply local\n450\tentropy-current monotonicity `∂_μ s^μ ≥ 0`, **without invoking\n451\tpointwise NEC**.\n452\t\n453\tThe bundle takes the entropy-current divergence as an\n454\t**externally-supplied real parameter** (`entropy_div`) and constrains\n455\tits sign to be non-negative — the Glorioso–Liu Eq. (3.20) content.\n456\tThe bundle also requires a positive-area horizon for cross-bundle\n457\tconsistency.\n458\t\n459\tThe KMS-Z₂ symmetry and unitarity (Im S_eff ≥ 0) of the SK-EFT\n460\teffective action are the *premises* of the Glorioso–Liu derivation;\n461\tthey enter as inputs to the (currently unformalized at the action\n462\tlevel) derivation and are recorded in the docstring as the\n463\tsubstrate-side hypothesis. Once the SK-EFT effective action is\n464\tformalized in Lean (deferred to Phase 6e for the nonlinear\n465\temergent-action), `KMS_Z2_symmetry_holds` and\n466\t`unitarity_ImS_nonneg` would become substantive predicates on a\n467\tformalized action functional. For now, the bundle ships with the\n468\ttwo substantive constraints below.\n469\t\n470\t**Two substantive fields (post-strengthening):**\n471\t- `entropy_divergence_nonneg`: `0 ≤ entropy_div` — the load-bearing\n472\t  Glorioso–Liu Eq. (3.20) constraint, parameterized over an\n473\t  externally-supplied entropy-current divergence.\n474\t- `horizon_area_link_consistent`: `0 < b.A` — bundle requires a\n475\t  positive-area horizon (independent of `BHData.A_pos` field as a\n476\t  consistency witness for use sites).\n477\t-/\n478\tstructure ADWSecondLaw (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) (entropy_div : ℝ) : Prop where\n479\t  entropy_divergence_nonneg    : 0 ≤ entropy_div\n480\t  horizon_area_link_consistent : 0 < b.A\n481\t\n482\t/-! ## §6 — Tracked-hypothesis bundle `H_RegimePartition`\n483\t\n484\t**Wave 5 load-bearing tracked hypothesis (corrected 2026-04-26-2230).**\n485\tThe ADW-substrate-specific partition critical mass `M_c` is project\n486\tansatz; the regime sign-of-dT_H/dt claims are primary-source-grounded:\n487\t\n488\t- **Schwarzschild branch** (`b.M > M_c p`): `dT_H/dt > 0` during\n489\t  evaporation. Standard Hawking 1975 result combined with\n490\t  `T_H_schwarzschild_strict_decreasing` (M↓ ⇒ T↑) and `dM/dt < 0`.\n491\t- **Acoustic branch** (`b.M < M_c p`): `dT_H/dt < 0` during\n492\t  evaporation. Balbinot 2005 Eq. Tsonic primary anchor; encoded\n493\t  via `T_H_acoustic_evolution_strict_decreasing`.\n494\t\n495\tThe rate `dT_dt_evap` is supplied as an **externally-supplied real\n496\tparameter** (not an existential), so the bundle constrains its sign\n497\twithout ∃-absorption.\n498\t\n499\tFive mutually-independent fields (anti-pattern-audit clean).\n500\t-/\n501\tstructure H_RegimePartition\n502\t    (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) (T_H0 : ℝ) (dT_dt_evap : ℝ) (delta : ℝ) : Prop where\n503\t  M_c_form_consistent          : 0 < M_c p\n504\t  T_H0_pos                     : 0 < T_H0\n505\t  evap_dT_dt_above             : b.M > M_c p → 0 < dT_dt_evap\n506\t  evap_dT_dt_below             : b.M < M_c p → dT_dt_evap < 0\n507\t  delta_consistent_with_ansatz : delta = (p.α_ADW - 1) * p.Λ_UV\n508\t\n509\t/-! ## §7 — `regime_partition_criterion` (Wave 5 correctness-push) -/\n510\t\n511\t/--\n512\t**Wave 5 correctness-push theorem (corrected).** Combines the regime\n513\tclassifier `classify` with the tracked hypothesis `H_RegimePartition`\n514\tto produce the explicit **sign-of-dT_H/dt-flips-at-M_c** statement.\n515\t\n516\tThis is the genuine regime-partition: in the Schwarzschild branch,\n517\tthe BH heats during evaporation (Hawking 1975 + textbook); in the\n518\tacoustic branch, the BH cools during evaporation (Balbinot 2005,\n519\tprimary anchor). The sign of `dT_H/dt` flips at `M_c`.\n520\t\n521\t**Anti-pattern audit.** Not ∃-absorption: the conditional sign claims\n522\tare over disjoint mass regions; both branches of the conjunction\n523\tencode primary-source-grounded physics on each side.\n524\t-/\n525\ttheorem regime_partition_criterion\n526\t    (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) (T_H0 dT_dt_evap delta : ℝ)\n527\t    (H : H_RegimePartition b p T_H0 dT_dt_evap delta) :\n528\t    (classify b p = .Schwarzschild → 0 < dT_dt_evap) ∧\n529\t    (classify b p = .ADWExtremality → dT_dt_evap < 0) := by\n530\t  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\n531\t  · intro hcls\n532\t    rw [classify_Schwarzschild_iff] at hcls\n533\t    exact H.evap_dT_dt_above hcls\n534\t  · intro hcls\n535\t    rw [classify_ADWExtremality_iff] at hcls\n536\t    exact H.evap_dT_dt_below hcls\n537\t\n538\t/--\n539\t**Substantive corollary.** Under the tracked-hypothesis bundle, the\n540\tsubstrate-response coefficient `δ` is *non-zero* iff `α_ADW ≠ 1`\n541\t(i.e., away from the bare Sakharov–Adler limit). This is the\n542\tconcrete falsifiability content of the deep-research §9 ansatz: a\n543\tmeasurement of `δ = 0` at `α_ADW ≠ 1` falsifies the ansatz.\n544\t-/\n545\ttheorem delta_ADW_nonzero_iff_alpha_ADW_ne_one\n546\t    (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) (T_H0 dT_dt_evap delta : ℝ)\n547\t    (H : H_RegimePartition b p T_H0 dT_dt_evap delta) :\n548\t    delta ≠ 0 ↔ p.α_ADW ≠ 1 := by\n549\t  rw [H.delta_consistent_with_ansatz]\n550\t  constructor\n551\t  · intro h hα\n552\t    apply h\n553\t    rw [hα]; ring\n554\t  · intro hα h\n555\t    apply hα\n556\t    have h1 : (p.α_ADW - 1) * p.Λ_UV = 0 := h\n557\t    rcases mul_eq_zero.mp h1 with h2 | h2\n558\t    · linarith\n559\t    · exact absurd h2 (ne_of_gt p.Λ_pos)\n560\t\n561\t/-! ## §8 — `FourLaws_*` Prop bundles (one per regime)\n562\t\n563\t**Post-Stage-13 strengthening note.** The original Wave 5 ship had\n564\t`FourLaws_*` bundles with five fields each, two of which (`zerothLaw_*`\n565\tand `thirdLaw_Israel_*`) were `True` placeholders. Stage 13 review\n566\tflagged this as a LeanProofSubstance BLOCKER: any Prop bundle with\n567\t`True` fields encodes no information in those slots. The post-rewrite\n568\tbundles ship **three substantive sign claims** plus an explicit\n569\tdisclosure that the zeroth- and third-law content is deferred to\n570\tPhase 6f.1+ (`Curvature.lean`, `ADMDecomposition.lean`) for proper\n571\tencoding. The deferred content is documented in the per-bundle\n572\tdocstrings; users reading the Wave 5 bundle understand exactly what\n573\tis and isn't encoded.\n574\t-/\n575\t\n576\t/--\n577\t**Schwarzschild-regime four laws (post-Stage-13 reduced bundle).** The\n578\tclassical Bardeen–Carter–Hawking laws applied to a BH with ADW\n579\temergent G_N. Three substantive Wave-5-formalizable fields:\n580\t\n581\t- `firstLaw_smarr`: `0 < p.G_N_emerg_eval` — the first law's coupling\n582\t  `1/(8π G_N)` requires G_N > 0.\n583\t- `secondLaw_Schw`: `ADWSecondLaw b p entropy_div` — SK-EFT entropy-\n584\t  current monotonicity (Glorioso–Liu).\n585\t- `evap_dT_dt_positive`: `0 < dT_dt_value` — Hawking 1975 sign,\n586\t  during evaporation `dT_H/dt > 0` (heats as it evaporates).\n587\t\n588\t**Deferred to Phase 6f+:**\n589\t- *zeroth law* (κ constant on horizon) — requires Killing-vector +\n590\t  horizon-generator infrastructure from `Curvature.lean` /\n591\t  `ADMDecomposition.lean`.\n592\t- *third law* (Israel strong form) — requires affine-time integral\n593\t  formalism from same Phase 6f infrastructure.\n594\t-/\n595\tstructure FourLaws_Schwarzschild\n596\t    (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) (dT_dt_value entropy_div : ℝ) : Prop where\n597\t  firstLaw_smarr                : 0 < p.G_N_emerg_eval\n598\t  secondLaw_Schw                : ADWSecondLaw b p entropy_div\n599\t  evap_dT_dt_positive           : 0 < dT_dt_value\n600\t\n601\t/--\n602\t**Acoustic-regime four laws (post-Stage-13 reduced bundle).\n603\t`ADWExtremality` constructor name retained for backward bibliographic\n604\tcontinuity, but the post-rewrite physics interpretation is\n605\tacoustic per Balbinot 2005.** Three substantive\n606\tWave-5-formalizable fields:\n607\t\n608\t- `firstLaw_smarr_with_substrate`: `0 < p.G_N_emerg_eval ∧\n609\t  delta = (p.α_ADW - 1) * p.Λ_UV` — the substrate-response correction\n610\t  to the Smarr identity (deep-research §9 ansatz).\n611\t- `secondLaw_ADWExt`: `ADWSecondLaw b p entropy_div` — SK-EFT\n612\t  entropy-current monotonicity.\n613\t- `evap_dT_dt_negative`: `dT_dt_value < 0` — Balbinot 2005 Eq. Tsonic,\n614\t  during evaporation `dT_H/dt < 0` (cools toward asymptotic\n615\t  extremality).\n616\t\n617\t**Deferred to Phase 6f+:**\n618\t- *zeroth law* (κ constant on horizon) — same dependency as\n619\t  Schwarzschild-regime bundle.\n620\t- *third law* (Israel/Reall BPS-conditional) — Reall (arXiv:2410.11956)\n621\t  BPS local mass-charge inequality + Kehle–Unger (arXiv:2211.15742)\n622\t  charged-scalar caveat; both require classical-GR infrastructure to\n623\t  encode the affine-time approach quantitatively. The Balbinot 2005\n624\t  `t ~ 1/T³` extrapolation gives the cooling-regime Israel-strong\n625\t  preservation prose-level.\n626\t-/\n627\tstructure FourLaws_ADWExtremality\n628\t    (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) (T_H0 delta dT_dt_value entropy_div : ℝ)\n629\t    : Prop where\n630\t  firstLaw_smarr_with_substrate : 0 < p.G_N_emerg_eval ∧\n631\t                                   delta = (p.α_ADW - 1) * p.Λ_UV\n632\t  secondLaw_ADWExt              : ADWSecondLaw b p entropy_div\n633\t  evap_dT_dt_negative           : dT_dt_value < 0\n634\t\n635\t/-! ## §9 — Wave 5 gating theorem -/\n636\t\n637\t/--\n638\t**Wave 5 gating theorem (corrected).** Combines the regime classifier\n639\twith the tracked-hypothesis bundle and the FourLaws bundle to produce\n640\tthe substantive structural claim:\n641\t\n642\t  In the acoustic regime (formally `.ADWExtremality`), the\n643\t  emergent BH satisfies the four laws (with the substrate-response\n644\t  first-law correction) AND the Hawking temperature has *negative*\n645\t  time-derivative under evaporation (cooling toward asymptotic\n646\t  extremality, per Balbinot 2005).\n647\t\n648\tBoth conjuncts are non-trivial: the post-strengthened\n649\t`FourLaws_ADWExtremality` bundle asserts three independent\n650\tsubstantive sign claims (firstLaw G_N + δ ansatz, secondLaw entropy\n651\tdivergence, evap dT/dt sign — with zeroth and third laws explicitly\n652\tdeferred to Phase 6f.1+ classical-GR infrastructure per the\n653\tdocstring), and `dT_H/dt < 0` is the regime-defining sign-inversion\n654\tclaim primary-source-grounded by Balbinot 2005 Eq. Tsonic.\n655\t-/\n656\ttheorem four_laws_consistent_with_acoustic_regime\n657\t    (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) (T_H0 dT_dt_evap delta entropy_div : ℝ)\n658\t    (H_part : H_RegimePartition b p T_H0 dT_dt_evap delta)\n659\t    (h_extr : classify b p = .ADWExtremality)\n660\t    (h_fl   : FourLaws_ADWExtremality b p T_H0 delta dT_dt_evap entropy_div) :\n661\t    FourLaws_ADWExtremality b p T_H0 delta dT_dt_evap entropy_div ∧\n662\t      dT_dt_evap < 0 := by\n663\t  rw [classify_ADWExtremality_iff] at h_extr\n664\t  refine ⟨h_fl, H_part.evap_dT_dt_below h_extr⟩\n665\t\n666\t/-! ## §10 — Falsifier theorems\n667\t\n668\tFour falsifiers anchored to primary-source-grounded predictions. Each\n669\tencodes a measurable observable whose specific outcome would falsify\n670\tthe wave's regime-partition ansatz.\n671\t-/\n672\t\n673\t/--\n674\t**Falsifier 1 — Acoustic-decay form falsifier (post-Stage-13 strengthened).**\n675\tThe acoustic regime predicts strict monotone-decay of `T_H(t)` per\n676\tBalbinot 2005 Eq. (Tsonic). A candidate `T_H_alt(t)` whose values match\n677\t`T_H_acoustic_evolution` at `t₁` AND `t₂` (both endpoints of an\n678\tevaporation interval) but does NOT decrease across the interval is\n679\tinconsistent with the strict-decreasing acoustic-evolution theorem.\n680\t\n681\tThis is non-tautological: the proof uses\n682\t`T_H_acoustic_evolution_strict_decreasing` to derive a contradiction\n683\tbetween the candidate's non-decrease and Balbinot's predicted strict\n684\tdecrease.\n685\t-/\n686\ttheorem falsifier_acoustic_decay_form\n687\t    {T_H0 τ_cool : ℝ} (hT0 : 0 < T_H0) (hτ : 0 < τ_cool)\n688\t    (T_H_alt : ℝ → ℝ) {t₁ t₂ : ℝ} (h_t : t₁ < t₂)\n689\t    (h_match_t1 : T_H_alt t₁ = T_H_acoustic_evolution T_H0 τ_cool t₁)\n690\t    (h_alt_nondec : T_H_alt t₁ ≤ T_H_alt t₂) :\n691\t    -- A candidate that matches Balbinot at t₁ AND fails to decrease\n692\t    -- by t₂ MUST disagree with Balbinot at t₂.\n693\t    T_H_alt t₂ ≠ T_H_acoustic_evolution T_H0 τ_cool t₂ := by\n694\t  intro h_eq_t2\n695\t  -- Balbinot at t₂ < Balbinot at t₁ (strict decrease)\n696\t  have h_dec : T_H_acoustic_evolution T_H0 τ_cool t₂\n697\t              < T_H_acoustic_evolution T_H0 τ_cool t₁ :=\n698\t    T_H_acoustic_evolution_strict_decreasing hT0 hτ h_t\n699\t  -- Substitute candidate matches at both endpoints\n700\t  rw [h_eq_t2] at h_alt_nondec\n701\t  rw [h_match_t1] at h_alt_nondec\n702\t  -- h_alt_nondec : Balbinot(t₁) ≤ Balbinot(t₂)\n703\t  -- h_dec       : Balbinot(t₂) < Balbinot(t₁)\n704\t  linarith\n705\t\n706\t/--\n707\t**Falsifier 2 — Schwarzschild-heating sign falsifier (post-Stage-13\n708\tstrengthened).** The Schwarzschild regime predicts `dT_H/dt > 0` during\n709\tevaporation (T_H ∝ 1/M, dM/dt < 0). Given an `H_RegimePartition`\n710\thypothesis bundle and a Schwarzschild-regime classification, an\n711\tobserved non-positive `dT_dt_evap` is inconsistent with the bundle's\n712\t`evap_dT_dt_above` field.\n713\t\n714\tThis is non-tautological: the proof uses BOTH the regime classification\n715\t(via `classify_Schwarzschild_iff`) and the bundle's sign-claim field\n716\tto derive a contradiction with the observation.\n717\t-/\n718\ttheorem falsifier_schwarzschild_heating\n719\t    (b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) (T_H0 dT_dt_evap delta : ℝ)\n720\t    (H : H_RegimePartition b p T_H0 dT_dt_evap delta)\n721\t    (h_Schw : classify b p = .Schwarzschild)\n722\t    (h_observed_nonpos : dT_dt_evap ≤ 0) :\n723\t    -- Contradiction: bundle says dT/dt > 0 in Schwarzschild regime,\n724\t    -- observation says dT/dt ≤ 0.\n725\t    False := by\n726\t  rw [classify_Schwarzschild_iff] at h_Schw\n727\t  have h_pos : 0 < dT_dt_evap := H.evap_dT_dt_above h_Schw\n728\t  linarith\n729\t\n730\t/--\n731\t**Falsifier 3 — Third-law-form falsifier (post-Stage-13 strengthened).**\n732\tThe acoustic regime predicts `t ~ 1/T³` per Balbinot 2005, hence\n733\tIsrael strong form: the approach time `τ_approach(ε)` to reach\n734\t`T_H = ε` is unbounded as `ε → 0`. Kehle–Unger (arXiv:2211.15742)\n735\tdemonstrates a charged-scalar-matter sector that violates this:\n736\t`τ_approach` is bounded above by some `τ_max` for all small enough ε.\n737\t\n738\tA theory cannot satisfy both: this falsifier proves the contradiction.\n739\tThe Israel-strong predicate is the strong form (uniformly unbounded\n740\ton a tail of small ε); the Kehle–Unger predicate is the bounded form.\n741\t\n742\t**Non-tautological proof.** Uses `min ε₀ ε₀'` to pick a concrete ε\n743\twhere both predicates apply, then derives a contradiction from\n744\tthe bundle's two-sided constraint.\n745\t-/\n746\ttheorem falsifier_third_law_form\n747\t    (τ_approach : ℝ → ℝ)\n748\t    (h_israel_strong :\n749\t      ∀ τ_max : ℝ, ∃ ε_th : ℝ, 0 < ε_th ∧\n750\t        ∀ ε, 0 < ε → ε ≤ ε_th → τ_max < τ_approach ε)\n751\t    (h_kehle_unger_bounded :\n752\t      ∃ τ_max ε₀ : ℝ, 0 < ε₀ ∧\n753\t        ∀ ε, 0 < ε → ε ≤ ε₀ → τ_approach ε ≤ τ_max) :\n754\t    False := by\n755\t  obtain ⟨τ_max, ε₀, hε₀_pos, hKU⟩ := h_kehle_unger_bounded\n756\t  obtain ⟨ε_th, hε_th_pos, hIsrael⟩ := h_israel_strong τ_max\n757\t  set ε := min ε₀ ε_th with hε_def\n758\t  have hε_pos : 0 < ε := lt_min hε₀_pos hε_th_pos\n759\t  have hε_le_ε₀ : ε ≤ ε₀ := min_le_left _ _\n760\t  have hε_le_ε_th : ε ≤ ε_th := min_le_right _ _\n761\t  have hKU_at_ε : τ_approach ε ≤ τ_max := hKU ε hε_pos hε_le_ε₀\n762\t  have hIsrael_at_ε : τ_max < τ_approach ε := hIsrael ε hε_pos hε_le_ε_th\n763\t  linarith\n764\t\n765\t/--\n766\t**Falsifier 4 — α_ADW dependence of substrate-response falsifier\n767\t(post-Stage-13 renamed; previously `falsifier_chi_vest_dependence`,\n768\twhich had a name/content mismatch — the Wave-5 §9 ansatz depends on\n769\tα_ADW and Λ_UV, NOT directly on χ_vest).**\n770\t\n771\tThe Wave 5 deep-research ansatz `δ_ADW = (α_ADW − 1) · Λ_UV` vanishes\n772\tin the bare Sakharov–Adler limit `α_ADW = 1` and is positive for\n773\t`α_ADW > 1`. A measurement of opposite sign falsifies this ansatz.\n774\t\n775\t**Anti-pattern audit.** Encodes a sign-prediction whose falsification\n776\trules out a specific functional form. Non-trivial because the\n777\tconclusion `0 < (α_ADW - 1) · Λ_UV` requires both `α_ADW > 1` and\n778\t`Λ_UV > 0` (the latter from the substrate's `Λ_pos` field, not\n779\tfrom the function's structure alone).\n780\t-/\n781\ttheorem falsifier_alpha_ADW_dependence\n782\t    (p : ADWParams) (h_alpha_above_one : 1 < p.α_ADW) :\n783\t    0 < (p.α_ADW - 1) * p.Λ_UV := by\n784\t  have h1 : 0 < p.α_ADW - 1 := by linarith\n785\t  exact mul_pos h1 p.Λ_pos\n786\t\n787\t/-! ## §11 — Bridge to Waves 1, 2, 3 -/\n788\t\n789\t/--\n790\t**Wave 1 bridge.** The first-law coupling `1/(8π G_N^emerg)` in both\n791\t`FourLaws_*` bundles uses Wave 1's `LinearizedEFE.G_N_emerg` evaluated\n792\tat the substrate parameters. Positivity of G_N^emerg propagates through\n793\tto both regime branches.\n794\t-/\n795\ttheorem wave1_bridge_G_N_emerg_pos\n796\t    (_b : BHData) (p : ADWParams) :\n797\t    0 < p.G_N_emerg_eval :=\n798\t  p.G_N_emerg_eval_pos\n799\t\n800\t/--\n801\t**Wave 3 bridge — concrete weak-Nernst at SU(2)_k (post-Stage-13\n802\tstrengthened).** In the acoustic regime, the Hawking temperature\n803\treaches zero asymptotically (Balbinot 2005 `t ~ 1/T³`), but the\n804\tentropy is *positive* — inherited concretely from Wave 3's\n805\tKaul–Majumdar `kaulMajumdarS` evaluated at the asymptotic-extremality\n806\tarea `A = 4 · G_N · exp(2)` (the same anchor used by Wave 3's\n807\t`kaulMajumdar_S_pos_at_e_squared`).\n808\t\n809\t**Strong Nernst is violated** at this anchor: `S = exp(2) − 3 > 0`,\n810\tnot zero. **Weak Nernst is preserved** (entropy is finite at T = 0).\n811\t\n812\tThis bridge actually calls `kaulMajumdarS` (Wave 3 import), not a\n813\tgeneric positivity placeholder. It closes the Stage-13 BLOCKER that\n814\tflagged the previous version as a \"phantom bridge\" (claimed Wave 3\n815\tlinkage in prose without actual Wave 3 import).\n816\t-/\n817\ttheorem wave3_bridge_kaul_majumdar_at_e_squared_anchor\n818\t    (G_N : ℝ) (hG : 0 < G_N) :\n819\t    0 < SKEFTHawking.BHEntropyMicroscopic.kaulMajumdarS\n820\t            (4 * G_N * Real.exp 2) G_N 0 ∧\n821\t    SKEFTHawking.BHEntropyMicroscopic.kaulMajumdarS\n822\t            (4 * G_N * Real.exp 2) G_N 0 ≠ 0 := by\n823\t  have h_pos := SKEFTHawking.BHEntropyMicroscopic.kaulMajumdar_S_pos_at_e_squared G_N hG\n824\t  exact ⟨h_pos, ne_of_gt h_pos⟩\n825\t\n826\t-- Note: the previous tautological theorem\n827\t-- `wave3_bridge_weak_nernst_holds_strong_nernst_violated` was retired\n828\t-- in the post-Stage-13 strengthening pass. The substantive content\n829\t-- (weak Nernst preserved, strong Nernst violated for the acoustic\n830\t-- regime at the asymptotic-extremality limit) is now encoded by\n831\t-- `wave3_bridge_kaul_majumdar_at_e_squared_anchor` above, which\n832\t-- actually imports `SKEFTHawking.BHEntropyMicroscopic` and calls\n833\t-- `kaulMajumdarS` at the SU(2)_k anchor area.\n834\t\n835\t/-! ## §12 — Module summary -/\n836\t\n837\t/--\n838\t**Wave 5 module summary marker (corrected ship 2026-04-26-2230).** This\n839\tmodule formalizes the BCH four laws + regime partition for emergent-\n840\tgravity ADW black holes, anchored on:\n841\t\n842\t- **Balbinot 2005** (gr-qc/0405098, PRD 71, 064019) for the acoustic\n843\t  cooling regime (`b.M < M_c`): `dT_H/dt < 0`, asymptotic extremality\n844\t  at infinite time, mirrors `src/wkb/backreaction.py`'s exponential\n845\t  approximation `κ(t) ~ κ_0 · exp(-t/τ_cool)`.\n846\t- **Hawking 1975** (CMP 43, 199) for the Schwarzschild heating regime\n847\t  (`b.M > M_c`): `dT_H/dt > 0`, finite t-evap, classical T_H = ℏ/(8πM).\n848\t- **Glorioso–Liu 2017** (arXiv:1612.07705) for the SK-EFT second law\n849\t  without NEC.\n850\t- **Project-original** `M_c = (N_f · Λ_UV)/(12π · α_ADW)` ansatz (Wave 5\n851\t  deep-research §3 dimensional analysis) is encoded as a tracked\n852\t  hypothesis, NOT a derivation.\n853\t\n854\tTheorem roster: `M_c_pos`, `classify_*_iff` (3), `T_H_acoustic_evolution_*`\n855\t(3), `T_H_schwarzschild_*` (2), `regime_partition_criterion`,\n856\t`delta_ADW_nonzero_iff_alpha_ADW_ne_one`, `four_laws_consistent_with_acoustic_regime`,\n857\t4 falsifiers, 2 cross-wave bridges.\n858\t\n859\t**Zero new axioms** (verified post-rewrite via `#print axioms` on\n860\t`regime_partition_criterion`: only `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound`).\n861\t-/\n862\ttheorem _wave5_module_summary_marker : True := trivial\n863\t\n864\tend SKEFTHawking.BHThermodynamicsFourLaws\n865\t"}]},"uuid":"8dce330f-a84a-432b-808e-ab894074c62d","timestamp":"2026-08-15T19:38:39.225Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"6da2e2f3-e12c-43c5-a3b9-f218aaccd598","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-desktop","cwd":"/Users/johnroehm/Programming/PythonEnvironments/Physics/Fluid-Based-Physics-Research/SK_EFT_Hawking","sessionId":"6cf37aa2-f1c7-4e33-a712-f17c2d75d99b","version":"2.1.229","gitBranch":"HEAD","slug":"swift-singing-llama"}

Ted Jacobson }\n32\t\\\\[15pt]\n33\tUniversity of Maryland\\\\\n34\tCollege Park\\\\\n35\tMaryland\\\\\n36\tUSA\\\\\n37\tE-mail: jacobson@physics.umd.edu\n38\t\\\\[15pt]\n39\t{\\bf Tatsuhiko
